selected_news.summary: Azerbaijan welcomes Sinirlioglu’s candidacy for UN secretary-general Türkiye Today
selected_news.source_headline: Azerbaijan welcomes Sinirlioglu’s candidacy for UN secretary-general
selected_news.article_text: Azerbaijan has welcomed the candidacy of Feridun Sinirlioglu, secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), for the top post at the United Nations. Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry spokesperson Ayhan Hacizade said so in a written statement on the selection of the next U.N. secretary-general. He said Baku “welcomes” Sinirlioglu’s nomination. Hacizade said the choice should rest on candidates’ professional qualifications, diplomatic experience and impartiality. He added that a candidate also needs the ability to build consensus among member states. He stressed that the selection process should be conducted in line with the U.N. Charter. Hacizade said Azerbaijan believes ongoing consultations and constructive dialogue among member states will produce an appropriate decision. In his words, that outcome would strengthen the U.N.’s capacity to respond more effectively to today’s global challenges. Sinirlioglu, a career Turkish diplomat, was elected OSCE secretary-general in December 2024 at the organization’s ministerial council meeting in Malta. He is the first Turkish citizen to hold that post. He previously served as Türkiye’s ambassador to the United Nations. Reports earlier in October said Türkiye was weighing whether to put him forward, and that he had discussed a possible bid on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. At the time, Türkiye had not formally nominated him. Under the U.N. process, the 15-member Security Council selects a candidate, and each of its five permanent members holds a veto. The 193-member General Assembly then gives final approval. The next secretary-general is due to take office on Jan. 1, 2027

selected_news.title: Şumer Ezgu, ABU Festivali’nde Cura’yı Çalacak
selected_news.summary: Folk artist Sumer Ezgu to represent Türkiye at ABU Music Festival in Sri Lanka Türkiye Today
selected_news.query: culture arts cinema music world news
selected_news.source_headline: Folk artist Sumer Ezgu to represent Türkiye at ABU Music Festival in Sri Lanka
selected_news.article_text: Folk music artist Sumer Ezgu will take Türkiye to the Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union (ABU) Music Festival in Colombo, Sri Lanka, on Nov. 2, where he will perform “Anadolu’dan Geldik” ("We Came from Anatolia") and play a 66-year-old cura, a small stringed instrument related to the saz. The ABU is a media association that promotes cooperation among broadcasters in the Asia-Pacific region. Colombo is the largest city of Sri Lanka. The festival, organized by the ABU, of which TRT is also a member, will bring together the musical cultures of different countries in the Asia-Pacific region. TRT is Türkiye’s public broadcaster. Ezgu, who started his music career at a young age, turned to music with the instruments his teacher-father bought him. He received music and notation training in Komotini, Greece, where he lived for two years because of his father’s job. After returning to Türkiye, Ezgu continued his musical work and, after passing the radio exam, served as a staff artist at TRT. After working at TRT for 15 years, the artist turned to broadcasting and prepared television programs such as “Ankara Ruzgari,” “Nazar Degmesin” and “Halkali Seker.” The artist has introduced Anatolia’s musical culture with the program “Sumer Ezgu ile Anadolu’dan Geldik,” broadcast on TRT Muzik in recent years, and has prepared 53 episodes so far. Anatolia is the peninsula that makes up most of Türkiye’s territory. Sumer Ezgu said that they travel to different regions of Anatolia to record local music and instruments, and that folk culture holds an important place for him. Saying he grew up with the sounds of the davul, zurna and baglama from childhood, Ezgu said he has taken part in folk dance and music festivals in different countries. The davul is a large double-headed drum, the zurna is a loud woodwind instrument, and the baglama is a long-necked stringed instrument. Explaining that they filmed in Mersin and Gaziantep as part of the program, Ezgu said they recorded Silifke’s local dances, Gaziantep’s barak tunes and the region’s distinctive instruments. Barak tunes are a style of folk melody from southeastern Türkiye. Stressing that they do this work to pass cultural heritage on to future generations, Ezgu said: “We are documenting Anatolia’s endless colors as we travel around it. In a way, we are doing compilation work.” He added: “In fact, we are filming a record of today and leaving a file for the future.” Saying he is happy to represent Türkiye at the festival in Sri Lanka, Ezgu said the event will bring different cultures together through music. Noting that he will perform “Anadolu’dan Geldik” at the festival, Ezgu said: “Taking part in this festival, and presenting Türkiye there as a color of Asia-Pacific, especially with the piece ‘Anadolu’dan Geldik,’ made me very happy. We have completed the preparations.” Ezgu said he has the 66-year-old cura of the late folk artist Ramazan Gungor from Fethiye, a district in Türkiye’s southwest: “I have the 66-year-old cura of the late folk artist Ramazan Gungor from Fethiye. I will play that three-stringed instrument at the festival too.” He continued: “Ramazan Gungor used to call it a ‘kopuz.’ I will take an instrument from Anatolia to the geography it came from and play it there. This will also be a cultural fusion.” Ezgu said he will continue to make every effort to promote cultural heritage
